name: MHRA extends Casgevy to ages five and over
summary: The MHRA extended the UK authorisation of Casgevy to children aged five and over with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
keyPoints: The MHRA extended the UK authorisation of the gene-editing treatment Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) to children aged five and over.
It is for severe sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
Casgevy was previously authorised in the UK for people aged 12 and over.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) can now be used in eligible children from the age of five with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia. Before this decision, the UK authorisation covered people aged 12 and over.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA describes both as serious inherited blood disorders.

The MHRA decision is separate from NHS access, which in England is decided through NICE.

source.title: MHRA approves gene-editing treatment for children aged five and over with serious inherited blood disorders
